result.topic_en: Proof using the continued fraction for tanh x and the convergent recurrences to derive asymptotic approximations of e^{2/a}+1 by rationals with odd or even denominators.
result.transcription:
Proof Taking the equation
$\tanh x = \frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^2}{3+}\frac{x^2}{5+}\frac{x^2}{7+}\cdots$
we see that
(6) $\frac{1}{2}(e^{\frac{2}{a}}+1) = \frac{1}{1-}\frac{1}{a+}\frac{1}{3a+}\frac{1}{5a+}\frac{1}{7a+}\cdots$
Now let
(7) $\begin{cases} u_1 = 1, & v_1 = 1; \\ u_2 = |a|, & v_2 = |a-1|; \end{cases}$
and
(8) $\begin{cases} u_{n+1} - u_{n-1} = (2n-1)|a|u_n; \\ v_{n+1} - v_{n-1} = (2n-1)|a|v_n. \end{cases}$
Then we have
(9) $\frac{1}{2}(e^{\frac{2}{a}}+1) = \frac{u_n}{v_n} + (-1)^{n-1}\left(\frac{1}{v_n v_{n+1}} - \frac{1}{v_{n+1}v_{n+2}} + \cdots\right)$.
It is easy to deduce from (8) that
(10) $\begin{cases} v_{n+1} \sim 2|a| n v_n, \\ \log v_n \sim n\log n. \end{cases}$
It follows from (9) and (10) that
(11) $e^{\frac{2}{a}}+1 - \frac{2u_n}{v_n} \sim \frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{|a| n v_n^2}$.
If a is even, $v_n$ is always odd. In this case choosing $N = v_n$ so that $n \sim \log N/\log\log N$ we see that
(12) $N(e^{\frac{2}{a}}+1) - 2u_n \sim \frac{(-1)^{n-1}\log\log N}{|a| N\log N}$.
If a is odd and n is odd, $v_n$ is again odd. Let $N = v_n$. Then
(13) $N(e^{\frac{2}{a}}+1) - 2u_n \sim \frac{\log\log N}{|a| N\log N}$.
If a is odd and n is even, then $v_n$ is even. Now we can choose $N = \frac{1}{2}v_n$ so that
(14) $N(e^{\frac{2}{a}}+1) - u_n \sim -\frac{\log\log N}{4|a| N\log N}$.
